content.overview: Articles 25 to 28 are the freedom-of-religion cluster. Article 25 guarantees to all persons freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health, and the other Part III provisions. It does not prevent the State from regulating secular activity associated with religious practice, or from providing for social welfare and reform, or throwing open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus. Article 26 gives every religious denomination, subject to public order, morality and health, the right to establish and maintain institutions, manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and own and administer property in accordance with law. Article 27 bars compulsion to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion. Article 28 restricts religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds, and regulates it in other institutions.
content.study: Separate individual freedom in Article 25 from denomination rights in Article 26. Use Article 27 for a tax, not a fee question left unverified. Use Article 28 for religious instruction in educational institutions, matched to how the institution is funded.

sections.heading: Article 25
sections.body: Individual freedom of conscience and religion, with express State regulatory and reform powers under 25(2).

enhancement.definition: Articles 25 to 28 protect conscience and religious practice, denomination affairs, freedom from religious taxes, and limits on religious instruction.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The freedoms are subject to public order, morality and health, and Article 25 is also subject to the other Part III provisions. State reform of secular activity is written into Article 25(2).
essentialIngredients: Limit of public order, morality and health
Article 25(2) secular regulation or social reform if pleaded
Article 27 tax specifically appropriated for a religion
Article 28 matched to the funding of the institution
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 25(1) is person-wide and includes propagation, not only profession. The opening subjects it to public order, morality, health and the other fundamental rights. Article 25(2) preserves social-welfare and reform laws and the throwing open of Hindu public religious institutions. The explanation treats Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists with Hindus for that clause and for carrying a kirpan as included in the Sikh profession of religion. Article 26 is denomination-based and its property right is in accordance with law. Article 27 is about compulsion to pay taxes the proceeds of which are specifically appropriated for a particular religion. Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in an institution wholly maintained out of State funds. Article 28(2) saves an endowment or trust that requires religious instruction even if administered by the State. Article 28(3) requires consent, or the guardian's consent in the case of a minor, in a recognised or State-aided institution.
examples: A denomination manages its ritual affairs. Article 26(b) is the clause, subject to public order, morality and health.
A compulsory levy is specifically appropriated to one religion. Article 27 is the plea.
A wholly State-funded school adds compulsory religious instruction. Article 28(1) applies.

Article 28(1) wholly State-funded vs Article 28(3) aided institution

keyTakeaways: Article 25 applies to all persons and includes propagation.
It is subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III rights.
Article 27 targets taxes appropriated for a particular religion.
Article 28 depends on how the institution is maintained.
